newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire says Uganda invades, Kampala denies charge.
newsitem.headline: Zaire says Uganda invades, Kampala denies charge.

text.p: Zaire said on Wednesday several thousand Ugandan troops had invaded its territory, but Uganda immediately dismissed the accusation as laughable.

A military high command statement said about 2,000 Ugandan troops had left the Zairean town of Fizi -- about 350 km (about 200 miles) southwest of the Ugandan border -- and were heading in the direction of Kalemie in mineral-producing Shaba province.

"It is absolute falsehood. It is in fact laughable that we would be so stupid as to openly send troops into Zaire. Even the geographical locations mentioned do not make sense," Hope Kivengere, spokeswoman for President Yoweri Museveni, told Reuters by telephone from Kampala.
"The Zairean statement lacks credibility. We have not sent any troops at all to Zaire," Kivengere added.

The Zairean statement said: "We have also observed the presence on the Uganda-Zaire border of 2,000 men transported in vehicles and armed with machineguns. These men crossed into Zaire after being supplied with petrol by the Ugandan state."
"A second group of Ugandan soldiers is trying to cross Lake Mobutu," it said.
Zaire made no mention of any fighting or any Zairean effort to contain the alleged invasion.

Diplomats in the capital Kinshasa said the positions of the Ugandan troops described by the statement, if true, would cast doubts on earlier claims by the Zaire army of retaking the town of Walikali from rebels.
The diplomats have reported troop movements from both Uganda and Rwanda in recent days but the numbers they quote are significantly smaller.

In the most comprehensive charge against the Kampala government, Zaire also said a brigade of Ugandan troops equipped with Russian-made anti-aircraft missiles had taken position at Beni about 50 km (35 miles) from the Ugandan border south of the strategic mining town Bunia.
It said 200 mercenaries from Eritrea, Ethiopia and Somalia landed in the last few days in Goma, the biggest Zairean town seized by rebels who started fighting the army last October.

Zaire accuses Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi of fighting alongside Zaire's ethnic Tutsis who took up arms after local authorities tried to expel them to Rwanda, their ancentral homeland. A vast stretch of border land is in rebel hands.
Rebel leaders say their objective is to overthrow the central governemt in Kinshsa. The government has launched a counter-offensive backed by hundreds of European mercenaries.
